  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">Thinking by Subtraction: 
<br class="ltx_break">Confidence-Driven Contrastive Decoding for LLM Reasoning</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Recent work on test-time scaling for large language model (LLM) reasoning typically assumes that allocating more inference-time computation uniformly improves correctness.
However, prior studies show that reasoning uncertainty is highly localized: a small subset of low-confidence tokens disproportionately contributes to reasoning errors and unnecessary output expansion.
Motivated by this observation, we propose Thinking by Subtraction, a confidence-driven contrastive decoding approach that improves reasoning reliability through targeted token-level intervention.
Our method, termed Confidence-Driven Contrastive Decoding (CCD), identifies low-confidence tokens (LC-tokens) during decoding and selectively intervenes at these positions.
To construct a contrastive reference, CCD replaces high-confidence tokens (HC-tokens) with semantically minimal placeholder symbols, yielding a deliberately confused contrastive distribution.
By subtracting this reference distribution at LC-token positions, CCD refines uncertain predictions without additional training or multiple reasoning trajectories.
Experimental results demonstrate that CCD consistently improves accuracy across multiple mathematical reasoning benchmarks and achieves higher correctness with substantially more concise outputs on challenging AIME-style tasks. By incurring only minimal key–value (KV) cache overhead, CCD serves as a resource-efficient alternative to uniform test-time scaling. Our findings suggest that targeted intervention at localized low-confidence states can stabilize the decoding process and enhance reasoning reliability without the need for extensive computational redundancy. Our code will be made available at: https://github.com/bolo-web/CCD.</p>
  
</div>
<div class="ltx_keywords">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_keywords">Keywords: </h6>Machine Learning, LLM Reasoning, Contrastive Decoding, ICML
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<figure id="S1.F1" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18232v1/intro.svg" id="S1.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/285;" width="476" height="285"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S1.F1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 1</span>: </span><span id="S1.F1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
Trajectory-level relationship between token confidence and final answer correctness.
Across 2,880 reasoning trajectories generated by Qwen3-8B on AIME24.
</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Recent progress in large language models (LLMs)  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Achiam et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2025a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Team et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dubey et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al., 2025</a>)</cite> has shown that increasing inference-time computation can substantially improve reasoning performance.
However, most test-time scaling strategies <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lightman et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Welleck et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zheng et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhao et al., 2025</a>)</cite> achieve these gains by uniformly expanding computation across the entire decoding process, often through longer deliberation chains or multiple reasoning trajectories.
While effective, such approaches incur significant computational overhead and tend to amplify unnecessary reasoning.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Motivated by these limitations, and by recent evidence that controlled modification of internal logit and attention distributions can enhance reasoning fidelity in LLMs <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Nguyen et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Karan and Du, 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tang et al., 2025a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tang et al., 2025b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhao et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, we explore an alternative direction that focuses on improving the quality of a single decoding trajectory, rather than allocating additional computation globally or generating multiple reasoning branches.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Unlike test-time scaling, contrastive decoding (CD) has recently emerged as a lightweight alternative for enhancing reasoning performance at inference time, without requiring additional training or multiple sampling paths <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chuang et al., 2023</a>)</cite>.
Existing CD-based methods improve generation quality by contrasting the main model with auxiliary distributions induced by weakened or perturbed contexts, thereby suppressing undesirable token candidates during decoding. These results highlight the effectiveness of contrastive signals for shaping model behavior at test time.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">However, prior CD-based approaches to reasoning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chuang et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">O’Brien and Lewis, 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Leng et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Phan et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhao et al., 2024a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lee et al., 2025</a>)</cite> typically apply contrastive signals uniformly across decoding steps, implicitly treating all tokens as equally uncertain.
Related efforts explore coarser-grained interventions, such as layer-wise contrastive control <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chuang et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, which operate at the representation level rather than targeting localized uncertainty during autoregressive decoding. In practice, autoregressive reasoning uncertainty is often highly localized to specific decision points (e.g., arithmetic operations or logical transitions), while many tokens are generated with high confidence. Consequently, indiscriminate application of contrastive decoding may dilute its impact on critical steps and incur unnecessary computation on already-certain predictions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Motivated by findings in DeepConf <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fu et al., 2025</a>)</cite> that predictive confidence is closely correlated with reasoning correctness, we ask whether contrastive decoding can be used to selectively intervene at low-confidence decoding states and improve reasoning by increasing predictive confidence at these positions.
While this analysis does not establish token-level causality, it indicates that low-confidence decoding states serve as reliable signals of unstable reasoning within a trajectory.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Based on this observation, we hypothesize that selectively improving token reliability at low-confidence decoding positions can mitigate downstream reasoning errors.
This motivates a decoding-time mechanism based on contrastive decoding, which identifies locally uncertain reasoning steps and intervenes only when necessary.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">In this work, we introduce a confidence-aware perspective on contrastive decoding that directly addresses this limitation.
Rather than treating CD as a global decoding strategy, we use token-level confidence as an explicit uncertainty signal to determine <em id="S1.p7.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">when</em> and <em id="S1.p7.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">where</em> contrastive decoding should be activated.
This selective formulation allows CCD to preserve stable reasoning behavior at high-confidence positions while focusing contrastive correction on locally uncertain steps.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p8.1" class="ltx_p">The main contributions can be summarized as follows:</p>
<ul id="S1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We introduce <span id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Confidence-Driven Contrastive Decoding (CCD)</span>, a decoding-time framework that unifies token-level confidence estimation with contrastive decoding to correct locally uncertain reasoning steps.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We propose a <span id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">selective intervention strategy</span> that activates contrastive decoding only at low-confidence chain-of-thought tokens, enabling fine-grained control and avoiding the uniform computational overhead of sampling-based or multi-trajectory methods.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We demonstrate that CCD is <span id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">training-free, model-agnostic, and efficient</span>, requiring no additional supervision or architectural changes, while introducing minimal and predictable inference-time overhead through bounded KV cache maintenance.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S1.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p9.1" class="ltx_p">In Section 2, we introduce <em id="S1.p9.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Confidence-Driven Contrastive Decoding</em> (CCD).
Section 3 presents empirical and statistical evaluations of CCD on multiple reasoning benchmarks.
Section 4 concludes the paper and discusses limitations and future directions.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Methodology</h2>

<section id="S2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.1 </span>Overview</h3>

<figure id="S2.F2" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18232v1/method.png" id="S2.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/229;" width="476" height="229" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S2.F2.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 2</span>: </span><span id="S2.F2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Overview of Confidence-Driven Contrastive Decoding (CCD).
The decoding process consists of four key components:
(1) online estimation of token-level confidence;
(2) confidence-driven token selection that partitions chain-of-thought tokens into low-confidence (LC) and high-confidence (HC) sets;
(3) contrastive decoding triggered at LC-CoT tokens to refine uncertain predictions;
and (4) dual key–value (KV) cache maintenance to support selective intervention without disrupting standard autoregressive decoding.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We propose <em id="S2.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Confidence-Driven Contrastive Decoding</em> (CCD), a decoding-time approach for improving the reliability of autoregressive reasoning in large language models.
CCD is motivated by the observation that reasoning errors tend to arise at locally uncertain decoding steps, where token-level predictive confidence is low and semantic constraints are weakened.
Rather than uniformly increasing inference-time computation, CCD performs targeted intervention only at such uncertain positions.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.2 </span>Preliminaries: Confidence-Based Uncertainty and Contrastive Decoding</h3>

<div id="S2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Token-Level Confidence.</span>
CCD leverages token-level predictive confidence as a control signal for identifying unstable decoding states.
Following prior work, the confidence at position <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> is defined as</p>
<table id="S2.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="C_{i}=-\frac{1}{k}\sum_{j=1}^{k}\log P_{i}(j)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>k</mi></mfrac><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>k</mi></munderover><mi>log</mi><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{i}=-\frac{1}{k}\sum_{j=1}^{k}\log P_{i}(j),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{i}(j)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{i}(j)</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the probability of the <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>-th most likely token and <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> is the number of top-ranked candidates.
Lower confidence values correspond to flatter predictive distributions and higher uncertainty.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Sliding-Window Confidence.</span>
Following prior work on sliding-window statistics <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fu et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, we maintain a sliding window of recent token-level predictive confidence at decoding step <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S2.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{win}}^{(t)}=\left\{C_{t-W},\dots,C_{t-1}\right\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mi>win</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>W</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{win}}^{(t)}=\left\{C_{t-W},\dots,C_{t-1}\right\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">This window provides a local estimate of confidence dynamics for adaptive decoding control.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Contrastive Decoding.</span>
To refine predictions at low-confidence steps, CCD employs contrastive decoding to reshape the local decoding distribution.
At decoding step <math id="S2.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, logits are computed from the original context <math id="S2.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and a contrastive context <math id="S2.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{c}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>c</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{c}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> as
<math id="S2.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\ell^{(1)}_{t}=\operatorname{logit}_{\theta}(\cdot\mid c_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>logit</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell^{(1)}_{t}=\operatorname{logit}_{\theta}(\cdot\mid c_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>
and
<math id="S2.SS2.p3.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\ell^{(2)}_{t}=\operatorname{logit}_{\theta}(\cdot\mid\tilde{c}_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>logit</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>c</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell^{(2)}_{t}=\operatorname{logit}_{\theta}(\cdot\mid\tilde{c}_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>.
The contrastive logits are then given by</p>
<table id="S2.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell^{\mathrm{cd}}_{t}=(1+\alpha)\,\ell^{(1)}_{t}-\alpha\,\ell^{(2)}_{t}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>cd</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell^{\mathrm{cd}}_{t}=(1+\alpha)\,\ell^{(1)}_{t}-\alpha\,\ell^{(2)}_{t},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.p3.2" class="ltx_p">with the resulting decoding distribution</p>
<table id="S2.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\mathrm{cd}}\!\left(y_{t}\mid c_{t},\tilde{c}_{t}\right)=\operatorname{softmax}\!\left(\ell^{\mathrm{cd}}_{t}\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>cd</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>c</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:3.720em;" width="3.720em"><mi>softmax</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>cd</mi></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\mathrm{cd}}\!\left(y_{t}\mid c_{t},\tilde{c}_{t}\right)=\operatorname{softmax}\!\left(\ell^{\mathrm{cd}}_{t}\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Overall, CCD operates entirely at decoding time, requires no additional training or multiple reasoning trajectories, and introduces minimal computational overhead, providing a simple and principled mechanism for uncertainty-aware reasoning during inference.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Confidence-Driven Token Selection.</span>
CCD performs token-level selection by partitioning chain-of-thought (CoT) tokens into two confidence-aware categories based on percentile statistics of recent decoding states.
Specifically, given the sliding-window confidence set <math id="S2.SS2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{win}}^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mi>win</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{win}}^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math>, we estimate adaptive quantile-based thresholds to distinguish <em id="S2.SS2.p5.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">low-confidence</em> and <em id="S2.SS2.p5.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">high-confidence</em> tokens.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">We use the threshold <math id="S2.SS2.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{cd}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{cd}</annotation></semantics></math> to identify Low-Confidence CoT tokens (<span id="S2.SS2.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LC-Tokens</span>), defined as tokens whose confidence falls below the <math id="S2.SS2.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{cd}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{cd}</annotation></semantics></math>-th quantile of <math id="S2.SS2.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{win}}^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mi>win</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{win}}^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math>. Such tokens indicate localized uncertainty in the reasoning trajectory and serve as intervention points for contrastive decoding:</p>
<table id="S2.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{I}^{\mathrm{cd}}_{t}=\mathbf{1}\!\left(C_{t}&lt;\tau_{cd}\ \wedge\ t\in\mathcal{R}\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝕀</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>cd</mi></msubsup><mo rspace="0.108em">=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><mo rspace="0.722em">∧</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{I}^{\mathrm{cd}}_{t}=\mathbf{1}\!\left(C_{t}&lt;\tau_{cd}\ \wedge\ t\in\mathcal{R}\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.p6.2" class="ltx_p">Here, <math id="S2.SS2.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the set of decoding steps corresponding to the model-generated reasoning region, excluding question tokens.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Using the threshold <math id="S2.SS2.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{rep}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{rep}</annotation></semantics></math>, we identify High-Confidence CoT tokens (<span id="S2.SS2.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">HC-Tokens</span>) as those above the <math id="S2.SS2.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{r}</annotation></semantics></math>-th quantile of <math id="S2.SS2.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{win}}^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mi>win</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{win}}^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math>. These tokens are considered semantically dominant and are selectively attenuated in the contrastive branch to prevent overconfident cues from dominating the refinement process:</p>
<table id="S2.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{I}^{\mathrm{rep}}_{t}=\mathbf{1}\!\left(C_{t}&gt;\tau_{rep}\ \wedge\ t\in\mathcal{R}\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝕀</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>rep</mi></msubsup><mo rspace="0.108em">=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub><mo rspace="0.722em">∧</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{I}^{\mathrm{rep}}_{t}=\mathbf{1}\!\left(C_{t}&gt;\tau_{rep}\ \wedge\ t\in\mathcal{R}\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p8.1" class="ltx_p">By deriving both LC- and HC-Tokens from local confidence percentiles, CCD dynamically adapts token selection to the evolving uncertainty profile of the decoding trajectory, avoiding reliance on fixed global thresholds.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.3 </span>Confidence-Driven Contrastive Decoding</h3>

<div id="S2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">CCD performs contrastive decoding selectively based on token-level predictive confidence.
The core principle is to intervene only at locally uncertain decoding steps, while preserving standard decoding behavior at confident steps.</p>
</div>
<section id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Contrastive Distribution Construction.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">At decoding step <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, when the predictive confidence <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> falls below a threshold, we construct a contrastive decoding distribution by masking high-confidence semantic anchors in the recent context.
Selected tokens are replaced with <em id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Placeholder Tokens</em> (e.g., <span id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">&lt;endoftext&gt;</span> or <span id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">&lt;vision_pad&gt;</span>), which preserve sequence structure while removing dominant semantic content, yielding a contrastive context that disrupts semantic anchoring without altering positional alignment.
Formally, let <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathbf{y}}_{&lt;t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐲</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathbf{y}}_{&lt;t}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the contrastive context obtained from <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{y}_{&lt;t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐲</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{y}_{&lt;t}</annotation></semantics></math> via placeholder substitution, and the corresponding contrastive logits are computed as</p>
<table id="S2.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{t}^{\mathrm{cd}}=f_{\theta}(\tilde{\mathbf{y}}_{&lt;t})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>cd</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐲</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{t}^{\mathrm{cd}}=f_{\theta}(\tilde{\mathbf{y}}_{&lt;t}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">which induces the contrastive decoding distribution.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Confidence-Driven Logit Subtraction.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The final logits used for token selection are defined as</p>
<table id="S2.E8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{t}^{\mathrm{final}}=\begin{cases}(1+\alpha)\,\ell_{t}^{\mathrm{main}}-\alpha\,\ell_{t}^{\mathrm{cd}},&amp;\text{if }C_{t}&lt;\tau_{cd}\ \wedge\ t\in\mathcal{R},\\[5.0pt]
\ell_{t}^{\mathrm{main}},&amp;\text{otherwise},\end{cases}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>final</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>main</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>cd</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mtext>if </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><mo rspace="0.722em">∧</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>main</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mtext>otherwise</mtext><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{t}^{\mathrm{final}}=\begin{cases}(1+\alpha)\,\ell_{t}^{\mathrm{main}}-\alpha\,\ell_{t}^{\mathrm{cd}},&amp;\text{if }C_{t}&lt;\tau_{cd}\ \wedge\ t\in\mathcal{R},\\[5.0pt]
\ell_{t}^{\mathrm{main}},&amp;\text{otherwise},\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{t}^{\mathrm{main}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>main</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{t}^{\mathrm{main}}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the logits produced from the original decoding context.
The resulting decoding distribution is given by</p>
<table id="S2.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\mathrm{ccd}}(y_{t})=\softmax\!\left(\ell_{t}^{\mathrm{final}}\right)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>ccd</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:3.720em;" width="3.720em"><mo lspace="0.1389em">softmax</mo></mpadded><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>final</mi></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\mathrm{ccd}}(y_{t})=\softmax\!\left(\ell_{t}^{\mathrm{final}}\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">from which standard decoding strategies are applied.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.4 </span>Theoretical Analysis</h3>

<div id="S2.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We now explain how CCD constructs an effective contrastive context, and why replacing
high-confidence tokens is a principled choice.</p>
</div>
<section id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">From Confidence Correction to Contrastive Distribution Construction.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Reasoning errors are concentrated at low-confidence decoding steps, where the predictive
distribution is flat and logit margins are small.
Since contrastive decoding sharpens the main distribution only when the contrastive distribution
is less confident (i.e., higher entropy), the key question becomes how to construct a contrastive
context that yields a deliberately confused reference distribution.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">CCD addresses this by selectively masking high-confidence tokens in the decoding history.
Let <math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{t}=(y_{1},\ldots,y_{t-1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{t}=(y_{1},\ldots,y_{t-1})</annotation></semantics></math> denote the original context and
<math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid c_{t})=\softmax(\ell_{\theta}(c_{t}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0em">softmax</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid c_{t})=\softmax(\ell_{\theta}(c_{t}))</annotation></semantics></math> the corresponding next-token distribution.
The contrastive context <math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{c}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>c</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{c}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is obtained by replacing high-confidence tokens with a
semantically neutral placeholder <math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{y}</annotation></semantics></math>, yielding logits
<math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{t}^{\mathrm{cd}}=\ell_{\theta}(\tilde{c}_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>cd</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>c</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{t}^{\mathrm{cd}}=\ell_{\theta}(\tilde{c}_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">High-Confidence Tokens as Semantic Anchors.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the hidden representation used to predict token <math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, with logits given by
<math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell=Wz_{t}+b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>W</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell=Wz_{t}+b</annotation></semantics></math>.
In a transformer decoder, <math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is obtained by contextualizing the embeddings of all previously generated tokens:</p>
<table id="S2.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t}=F_{\theta}\!\big(E(y_{1}),\ldots,E(y_{t-1})\big)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}=F_{\theta}\!\big(E(y_{1}),\ldots,E(y_{t-1})\big),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the token embedding function and <math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{\theta}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{\theta}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> represents the transformer with parameters <math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Tokens with high predictive confidence typically correspond to sharply peaked conditional
distributions and receive large attention weights at future steps.
Denoting the attention weight on token <math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> by</p>
<table id="S2.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{t,i}=\softmax\!\left(\frac{q_{t}^{\top}k_{i}}{\sqrt{d}}\right)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:3.720em;" width="3.720em"><mo lspace="0.1389em">softmax</mo></mpadded><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><msqrt><mi>d</mi></msqrt></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{t,i}=\softmax\!\left(\frac{q_{t}^{\top}k_{i}}{\sqrt{d}}\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">high-confidence tokens often satisfy <math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{t,i}\gg a_{t,j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>≫</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{t,i}\gg a_{t,j}</annotation></semantics></math> for most <math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j\neq i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j\neq i</annotation></semantics></math>.
Such tokens act as <em id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">semantic anchors</em>, strongly constraining the mapping from context to logits.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Masking Anchors Increases Uncertainty.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Masking a high-confidence token replaces its embedding <math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{i}=E(y_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{i}=E(y_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> with a placeholder
<math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{e}_{i}=E(\tilde{y})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>e</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{e}_{i}=E(\tilde{y})</annotation></semantics></math>, inducing a perturbation <math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta e_{i}=\tilde{e}_{i}-e_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>e</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta e_{i}=\tilde{e}_{i}-e_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>.
A first-order expansion yields</p>
<table id="S2.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t}(\tilde{c}_{t})-z_{t}(c_{t})\;\approx\;J_{t,i}\,\Delta e_{i},\qquad J_{t,i}=\frac{\partial z_{t}}{\partial e_{i}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>c</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">≈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}(\tilde{c}_{t})-z_{t}(c_{t})\;\approx\;J_{t,i}\,\Delta e_{i},\qquad J_{t,i}=\frac{\partial z_{t}}{\partial e_{i}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">For anchor tokens, <math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{t,i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>J</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{t,i}</annotation></semantics></math> has large norm because attention routes information through <math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>,
leading to a substantial change in <math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and hence in the output logits.
Removing anchor information reduces the mutual information between the context and the next token,</p>
<table id="S2.E13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(Y_{t};\tilde{C}_{t})\leq I(Y_{t};C_{t})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>C</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(Y_{t};\tilde{C}_{t})\leq I(Y_{t};C_{t}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(13)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.3" class="ltx_p">which equivalently implies higher conditional entropy,</p>
<table id="S2.E14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H(Y_{t}\mid\tilde{C}_{t})\geq H(Y_{t}\mid C_{t})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>C</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(Y_{t}\mid\tilde{C}_{t})\geq H(Y_{t}\mid C_{t}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(14)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.4" class="ltx_p">As a result, the top-logit margin
<math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{t}=\ell_{t}^{(1)}-\ell_{t}^{(2)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{t}=\ell_{t}^{(1)}-\ell_{t}^{(2)}</annotation></semantics></math>
is reduced in expectation under contrastive decoding,
i.e., <math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{t}^{\mathrm{cd}}&lt;\Delta_{t}^{\mathrm{main}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>cd</mi></msubsup><mo>&lt;</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>main</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{t}^{\mathrm{cd}}&lt;\Delta_{t}^{\mathrm{main}}</annotation></semantics></math>,
leading to a flatter and more uncertain reference distribution.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">By masking high-confidence tokens when constructing the contrastive reference, we deliberately induce a more confused reference distribution that reflects disrupted semantic anchoring.
Subtracting this distribution during contrastive decoding sharpens predictions at low-confidence positions, thereby increasing token-level confidence and stabilizing the reasoning trajectory.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.5 </span>Dual KV Cache Maintenance</h3>

<div id="S2.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To support contrastive decoding while preserving the original generation trajectory, CCD maintains two parallel key–value (KV) cache states: a main cache <math id="S2.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{KV}_{t}^{\mathrm{main}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>KV</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>main</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{KV}_{t}^{\mathrm{main}}</annotation></semantics></math> and a contrastive cache <math id="S2.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{KV}_{t}^{\mathrm{cd}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>KV</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>cd</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{KV}_{t}^{\mathrm{cd}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The main cache follows standard autoregressive decoding, whereas the contrastive cache encodes a deliberately weakened contextual state used solely for generating contrastive predictions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">During decoding steps within the reasoning phase <math id="S2.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}</annotation></semantics></math>, the contrastive cache selectively attenuates locally confident tokens by replacing them with a semantically neutral placeholder.
Formally, the contrastive KV update is defined as</p>
<table id="S2.E15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{KV}_{t}^{\mathrm{cd}}=\begin{cases}\mathrm{KV}(\tilde{y}),&amp;C_{t}&gt;\tau_{rep}\ \wedge\ t\in\mathcal{R},\\[3.00003pt]
\mathrm{KV}(y_{t}),&amp;\text{otherwise},\end{cases}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>KV</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>cd</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mi>KV</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub><mo rspace="0.722em">∧</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mi>KV</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mtext>otherwise</mtext><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{KV}_{t}^{\mathrm{cd}}=\begin{cases}\mathrm{KV}(\tilde{y}),&amp;C_{t}&gt;\tau_{rep}\ \wedge\ t\in\mathcal{R},\\[3.00003pt]
\mathrm{KV}(y_{t}),&amp;\text{otherwise},\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(15)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.SS5.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{y}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes a <em id="S2.SS5.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Placeholder Token</em> as defined above.
Replacing selected tokens with placeholders removes dominant semantic content in the contrastive branch without modifying the decoding procedure.
As a result, CCD introduces only limited overhead by maintaining a single additional contrastive branch with its own KV cache of the same size as standard decoding, while all contrastive operations are performed at the logit level without extra attention passes or model evaluations.</p>
</div>
</section>

<math id="alg1.l12.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{cd}\leftarrow\mathrm{Quantile}(\mathcal{C},q_{cd})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mi>Quantile</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{cd}\leftarrow\mathrm{Quantile}(\mathcal{C},q_{cd})</annotation></semantics></math>

<div id="alg1.l13" class="ltx_listingline">
              
              
              <span id="alg1.l13.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">else</span>


</div>
<div id="alg1.l14" class="ltx_listingline">
              
              
               <math id="alg1.l14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{rep}\leftarrow+\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{rep}\leftarrow+\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="alg1.l14.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{cd}\leftarrow-\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{cd}\leftarrow-\infty</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l15" class="ltx_listingline">
              
              
              <span id="alg1.l15.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">end</span> <span id="alg1.l15.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">if</span>
</div>
<div id="alg1.l16" class="ltx_listingline">
              
              
              <math id="alg1.l16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{I}_{t}^{\mathrm{rep}}\leftarrow\mathbf{1}(t\in\mathcal{R}\wedge C_{t}&gt;\tau_{rep})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝕀</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>rep</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mn>𝟏</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>∧</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{I}_{t}^{\mathrm{rep}}\leftarrow\mathbf{1}(t\in\mathcal{R}\wedge C_{t}&gt;\tau_{rep})</annotation></semantics></math>

<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Empirical and Statistical Evaluation</h2>

<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Experimental Setup</h3>

<section id="S3.SS1.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">3.1.1 </span>Benchmarks</h4>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We conduct experiments on four competitive mathematical reasoning benchmarks:
AIME 2024 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Art of Problem Solving, 2024a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Art of Problem Solving, 2024b</a>)</cite>,
AIME 2025 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Art of Problem Solving, 2025a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">Art of Problem Solving, 2025b</a>)</cite>,
BRUMO 2025 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">BRUMO, 2025</a>)</cite>,
and HMMT 2025 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">HMMT, 2025</a>)</cite>.
These benchmarks consist of Olympiad-style problems that require multi-step symbolic manipulation and precise logical reasoning.
They have been widely adopted to assess the reasoning capabilities of recent large language models, including Qwen3 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2025b</a>)</cite>, Grok-4 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">xAI, 2025</a>)</cite>, and GPT-5 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">OpenAI, 2025</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS1.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">3.1.2 </span>Models</h4>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate <em id="S3.SS1.SSS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Confidence-Driven Contrastive Decoding</em> (CCD) on a range of recent open-weight large language models spanning diverse parameter scales.
Specifically, we consider Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-14B and Qwen3-32B from the Qwen3 family <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">Qwen Team, 2025b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib50" title="" class="ltx_ref">Qwen Team, 2025c</a>; <a href="#bib.bib51" title="" class="ltx_ref">Qwen Team, 2025a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib48" title="" class="ltx_ref">Qwen Team, 2025d</a>)</cite>, as well as DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib52" title="" class="ltx_ref">DeepSeek-AI, 2025</a>)</cite>.
All models are evaluated in their original pretrained or distilled forms, without any additional fine-tuning.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS1.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">3.1.3 </span>Implementation Details</h4>

<section id="S3.SS1.SSS3.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Decoding Baselines.</h5>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We compare CCD against standard top-<math id="S3.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> sampling with <math id="S3.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p{=}0.95" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.95</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p{=}0.95</annotation></semantics></math> and temperature-based sampling.
Unless otherwise specified, baseline decoding uses temperature sampling with the temperature set to <math id="S3.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.6</annotation></semantics></math>.
All decoding methods generate a single reasoning trajectory per input, and no test-time ensembling or self-consistency is applied.
For MTI <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2025c</a>)</cite>, we follow the decoding configuration reported in the original paper.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Main Results</h3>

<section id="S3.SS2.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">3.2.1 </span>Overall Performance</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 3.2.1 Overall Performance ‣ 3.2 Main Results ‣ 3 Empirical and Statistical Evaluation ‣ Thinking by Subtraction: Confidence-Driven Contrastive Decoding for LLM Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> reports the main results of CCD on four competitive mathematical reasoning benchmarks.
Across most datasets and model scales, CCD consistently outperforms the Base decoding strategy and achieves performance comparable to MTI.
In particular, CCD yields stable improvements on both AIME-style benchmarks and more diverse reasoning sets such as BRUMO25 and HMMT25.
On Qwen dense models ranging from 4B to 14B parameters, CCD improves Mean8 accuracy by approximately 3–5% over the Base method, demonstrating consistent gains across model scales.
Overall, these results indicate that CCD provides a stable improvement over standard decoding under a unified confidence-driven framework.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S3.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 3.2.1 Overall Performance ‣ 3.2 Main Results ‣ 3 Empirical and Statistical Evaluation ‣ Thinking by Subtraction: Confidence-Driven Contrastive Decoding for LLM Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> further reports the gains of CCD over the Base setting across both mixture-of-experts and dense model variants.
Consistent improvements are observed for MoE models as well as smaller dense models such as DeepSeek-R1-1.5B, suggesting that CCD generalizes well across architectures and model sizes.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.T1" class="ltx_table">
<table id="S3.T1.3" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
